questions.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned}2v+3w=10 \\ v-\frac{3}{4}w=5\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $4.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2v+3w=10 \\ v-\frac{3}{4}w=5 & |\,\times 4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}2v+3w=10 \\ 4v-3w=20\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $3w$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-3w$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $w$-variable, and allows us to solve for $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2v+\cancel{3w} & =10 \\ 4v-\cancel{3w} & =20 \\ 6v & =30 \\ v & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $v=5$ into the equation $4v-3w=20$ to solve for $w:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4v-3w & =20 \\ 4\cdot 5-3w & =20 \\ 20-3w & =20 \\ -3w & =0 \\ w & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $v=5$ and $w=0.$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}-5x-9y=-12 \\ \frac{5}{6}x-2y=9\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}-5x-9y=-12 \\ \frac{5}{6}x-2y=9 & |\,\times 6\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}-5x-9y=-12 \\ 5x-12y=54\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $-5x$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $5x$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable, and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{5x}-9y & =-12 \\ \cancel{5x}-12y & =54 \\ -21y & =42 \\ y & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=-2$ into the equation $-5x-9y=-12$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5x-9y & =-12 \\ -5x-9\cdot (-2) & =-12 \\ -5x+18 & =-12 \\ -5x & =-30 \\ x & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=6,\,y=-2.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution to the  following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{1}{3}y=2 \\ \frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{4}y=1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $4,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{1}{3}y=2 & |\times 3 \\ \frac{1}{2}x-\frac{1}{4}y=1 & |\times 4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}6x-y=6 \\ 2x-y=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $y$ term that can cancel with the $-y$ term in the first equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}6x-y=6 &  \\ 2x-y=4 & |\,\times (-1)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}6x-y=6 \\ -2x+y=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable, and allows us to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-\cancel{y} & =6 \\ -2x+\cancel{y} & =-4 \\ (6x-2x) & =(6-4) \\ 4x & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{4} \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=\frac{1}{2}$ into the second equation to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y & =4 \\ 2(\frac{1}{2})-y & =4 \\ 1-y & =4 \\ y & =1-4 \\ y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=\frac{1}{2},\,y=-3.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}a+b=-3 \\ a-\frac{1}{3}b=-9\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $3,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}a+b=-3 & |\times 4 \\ a-\frac{1}{3}b=-9 & |\times 3\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3a+4b=-12 \\ 3a-b=-27\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-3a$ term that can cancel with the $3a$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3a+4b=-12 & |\,\times (-1) \\ 3a-b=-27 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}-3a-4b=12 \\ 3a-b=-27\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $a$-variable, and allows us to solve for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{3a}-4b & =12 \\ \cancel{3a}-b & =-27 \\ (-4b-b) & =(12-27) \\ -5b & =-15 \\ b & =\frac{-15}{-5} \\ b & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $b=3$ into the second equation to solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3a-b & =-27 \\ 3a-3 & =-27 \\ 3a & =-24 \\ a & =-\frac{24}{3} \\ a & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $a=-8,\,b=3.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}v-2w=5 \\ -v-\frac{2}{5}w=5\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $5,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}v-2w=5 & |\times 3 \\ -v-\frac{2}{5}w=5 & |\times 5\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}5v-6w=15 \\ -5v-2w=25\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $v$ by adding the two equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{5v}-6w & =15 \\ -\cancel{5v}-2w & =25 \\ (-6w-2w) & =(15+25) \\ -8w & =40 \\ w & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $w=-5$ into the first equation to solve for $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5v-6w & =15 \\ 5v-6(-5) & =15 \\ 5v+30 & =15 \\ 5v & =-15 \\ v & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $v=-3,\,w=-5.$

$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $t$ in the first equation:

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $s=4,\,t=-1.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6}+\frac{5y}{6}-2=0 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6}+\frac{5y}{6}-2=0 & |\,\times 6 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x+5y-12=0 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the second equation can easily be solved for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+y+6 & =0 \\ y & =-3x-6\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $y=-3x-6$ into the first equation and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5y-12 & =0 \\ x+5(-3x-6)-12 & =0 \\ x-15x-30-12 & =0 \\ -14x-42 & =0 \\ -14x & =42 \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $y,$ we substitute $x=-3$ into the equation $y=-3x-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3x-6 \\  & =-3(-3)-6 \\  & =9-6 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-3,\,y=3.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{7}+\frac{2y}{7}=1 \\ x-y=1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $7.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{7}+\frac{2y}{7}=1 & |\,\times 7 \\ x-y=1\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x+2y=7 \\ x-y=1\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $x$ in the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y & =1 \\ x & =1+y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $x=1+y$ into the first equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & =7 \\ (1+y)+2y & =7 \\ 1+3y & =7 \\ 3y & =6 \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=2$ into the equation $x=1+y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1+y \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=3,\,y=2.$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3-4x \\  & =-3-4(-2) \\  & =-3+8 \\  & =5\end{aligned}

{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{7}{3}y=2 & |\times 3 \\ x+\frac{4}{7}y=-\frac{3}{7} & |\times 7\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x+7y=6 \\ 7x+4y=-3\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the first equation can easily be solved for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+7y & =6 \\ x & =6-7y\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $x=6-7y$ into the second equation and then solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7x+4y & =-3 \\ 7(6-7y)+4y & =-3 \\ 42-49y+4y & =-3 \\ -45y & =-45 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=1$ into the equation $x=6-7y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =6-7y\text{ } \\  & =6-7(1) \\  & =6-7 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-1$ and $y=1.$

questions.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{6}v-\frac{1}{6}w=2 \\ \frac{2}{5}v+\frac{1}{5}w=2\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$v=$
{{field-1}}$,\,w=$
{{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $6$ and the second equation by $5,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{6}v-\frac{1}{6}w=2 & |\times 6 \\ \frac{2}{5}v+\frac{1}{5}w=2 & |\times 5\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}4v-w=12 \\ 2v+w=10\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the second equation can easily be solved for $w:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2v+w & =10 \\ w & =10-2v\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $w=10-2v$ into the first equation and then solve for $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4v-w & =12 \\ 4v-(10-2v) & =12 \\ 4v-10+2v & =12 \\ 6v & =22 \\ v & =\frac{22}{6} \\ v & =\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $w,$ we substitute $v=\frac{11}{3}$ into the equation $w=10-2v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =10-2v\text{ } \\  & =10-2(\frac{11}{3}) \\  & =10-\frac{22}{3} \\  & =\frac{30-22}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $v=\frac{11}{3}$ and $w=\frac{8}{3}.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution to the  following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}u-\frac{1}{3}w=\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{5}u-\frac{1}{2}w=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $6$ and the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}u-\frac{1}{3}w=\frac{1}{2} & |\times 6 \\ \frac{1}{5}u-\frac{1}{2}w=\frac{2}{5} & |\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}u-2w=3 \\ 2u-5w=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the first equation can easily be solved for $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u-2w & =3 \\ u & =2w+3\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $u=2w+3$ into the second equation and then solve for $w:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2u-5w & =4 \\ 2(2w+3)-5w & =4 \\ 4w+6-5w & =4 \\ -w+6 & =4 \\ -w & =-2 \\ w & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $u,$ we substitute $w=2$ into the equation $u=2w+3$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =2w+3 \\  & =2(2)+3 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $u=7$ and $w=2.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a System Containing Fractions in One Equation Using Elimination
canonical_examples.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}-x-5y=-1 \\ \frac{1}{4}x+3y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $4.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}-x-5y=-1 \\ \frac{1}{4}x+3y=2 & |\,\times 4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $-x$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $x$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable, and allows us to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{x}-5y & =-1 \\ \cancel{x}+12y & =8 \\ 7y & =7 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=1$ into the equation $-x-5y=-1$ to solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}-x-5y & =-1 \\ -x-5\cdot 1 & =-1 \\ -x-5 & =-1 \\ -x & =4 \\ x & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-4, \, y=1.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a System Containing Fractions in Both Equations Using Elimination
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}x+2y=3 \\ \frac{1}{6}x-\frac{2}{3}y=-7\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second equation by $6,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}x+2y=3 & |\times 2 \\ \frac{1}{6}x-\frac{2}{3}y=-7 & |\times 6\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $y$ by adding the two equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+\cancel{4y} & =6 \\ x-\cancel{4y} & =-42 \\ (5x+x) & =(6-42) \\ 6x & =-36 \\ x & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-6$ into the second equation to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x-4y & =-42 \\ -6-4y & =-42 \\ -4y & =-36 \\ y & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=-6$ and $y=9.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a System Containing Fractions in One Equation Using Substitution
canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=-4 \\ x-\frac{y}{6}=\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y=-4 \\ x-\frac{y}{6}=\frac{5}{2} & |\,\times 6\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $x$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & =-4 \\ x & =-4-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $x=-4-2y$ into the second equation and solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-y & =15 \\ 6(-4-2y)-y & =15 \\ -24-12y-y & =15 \\ -24-13y & =15 \\ -13y & =39 \\ y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=-3$ into the equation $x=-4-2y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-4-2y \\  & =-4-2(-3) \\  & =-4+6 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x = 2$ and $y = -3.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Solving a System Containing Fractions in Both Equations
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the solution to the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5a+\frac{3b}{2}=2 \\ \frac{4a}{3}+2b=0\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions, we multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second equation by $3,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5a+\frac{3b}{2}=2 & |\,\times 2 \\ \frac{4a}{3}+2b=0 & |\,\times 3\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-2,$ then we will get a $-6b$ term that can cancel with the $6b$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}10a+3b=4 & |\,\times (-2) \\ 4a+6b=0 & \end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $b$-variable, and allows us to solve for $a\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}-20a-\cancel{6b} & =-8 \\ 4a+\cancel{6b} & =0 \\ (-20a+4a) & =(-8+0) \\ -16a & =-8 \\ a & =\frac{-8}{-16} \\ a & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $a=\dfrac{1}{2}$ into the equation $4a+6b=0$ to solve for $b\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}4a+6b & =0 \\ 4(\frac{1}{2})+6b & =0 \\ 2+6b & =0 \\ 6b & =-2 \\ b & =-\frac{2}{6} \\ b & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a = \dfrac{1}{2}, \,b =-\dfrac{1}{3}.$
